page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance designed for accelerated computation and machine learning tasks. Built on the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 architecture, it features an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 vCPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, supported by a 40 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 60.0 GB of RAM (7.5 GB per vCPU), and the server includes 472 GB of local SSD storage alongside a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Hardware acceleration is powered by a single NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. Benchmark performance indicates strong GPU-focused throughput, reaching top-tier results in LLM prompt processing for small (9872.83 tokens/sec) and medium models (316.69 tokens/sec), along with strong text generation output (42.77 tokens/sec on 7B models). Conversely, the host Broadwell-generation CPU delivers modest single-core and multi-core performance, scoring in the bottom percentiles across general integer, compression, and memory bandwidth tests.

This hardware balance dictates clear tradeoffs. While local SSD storage provides immediate low-latency disk space and the P100 remains capable for medium-scale deep learning models, the legacy CPU platform bottlenecks general data processing, encryption, and in-memory key-value operations like Redis. Cost efficiency is highest when software pipelines offload the majority of computation directly to the GPU rather than relying heavily on host CPU execution. The server is primarily suitable for deep learning inference, Pascal-compatible GPU acceleration, computer vision tasks, and lightweight AI model evaluation.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance featuring 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores) on an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor at 2.5 GHz, 60.0 GB of system RAM, and 472 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Computational acceleration is delivered by a dedicated NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, running on KVM virtualization with 3 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier LLM prompt processing and solid text generation for small to medium models, though host CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into lower percentiles due to the legacy processor generation. The instance delivers optimal resource efficiency when tasks offload heavily to the GPU, making it well fitted for AI inference, batch video rendering, and deep learning model workloads.
